_about: Charles Rollin (1661-1741), rector of the University of Paris, in the standard anonymous English translations: the Ancient History in the six-volume London edition (Vol. I clean Gutenberg from the 1850 Longman printing; Vols. II, IV-VI from the same 1850 printing and Vol. III from William Tegg's 1851 issue, which divides the books identically: I-III, IV-VII, VIII-XII, XIII-XVI, XVII-XIX, XX-XXIV); the History of the Arts and Sciences of the Antients (1768, 3 vols); the Roman History to Actium (London 1754, 16 vols; Rollin died in 1741 mid-work and Crevier finished it: Vol. IX's title page reads 'continued and completed by Mr Crevier', and Vols. IX-XVI are tagged so; this second edition calls itself 'translated from the French'); and the Method of Teaching and Studying the Belles Lettres (1778, 4 vols). Eighteenth-century volumes are ECCO-style scans with long-s OCR. Classical scholarship (lane B, round dg). Raw IA OCR except Vol. I of the Ancient History. No uids minted.
